clue.text: Aid to modesty on the beach is a cause of distress when invaded by object at the speed of sound

definitions.text: Aid to modesty on the beach

indicators.note: something invaded by other pieces has them placed inside it, so the outer word is broken open

parts.note: a bane is a source of misery or distress
an object is a thing
Mach 1, written MACH I, is the speed of sound

explanation.surface: Something meant to protect beachgoers' modesty turns into a nuisance when a supersonic object crashes into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when invaded by' puts THING and MACH I (Mach 1, the speed of sound, with I for one) inside BANE. Victorian bathers changed in a wheeled hut drawn into the sea so as not to be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Victorian bathers undressed inside a wheeled hut pushed into the sea, keeping them out of public view.

clue.text: Possibly a quiz within a quiz, possibly a game of cards

indicators.note: within means the shuffled piece sits inside the other piece

parts.note: a bee is a quiz contest, as in a spelling bee

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of the word quiz could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A quiz nested in another quiz turns out to be a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' turns QUIZ into ZIQU, which sits 'within' BEE, as in a spelling bee.
explanation.definitionFit: Bezique is a nineteenth-century trick-taking card game for two players, played with a double pack.

clue.text: Hour passed in talk

explanation.definitionFit: An hour on the clock tells what o'clock it is; and to 'pass the time of day' is to chat briefly with someone.

clue.text: Island, one putting business first

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
biz is slang for business, as in showbiz
A is first, as in A1 or grade A

explanation.surface: An island where people put business before all else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' is a link; the pieces stand in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is one of the Balearic islands in the Mediterranean, off Spain.

clue.text: Topped with parsley out of his garden

indicators.note: out of signals the letters are taken out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A dish is finished with parsley picked from his own garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish decorated with a herb sprinkled on top has been dressed for serving.

clue.text: See 1
Parent and child in the building trade

parts.note: ma is a mother, a parent
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A mother and her son work together on building sites.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason cuts and lays stone, a craft of the construction industry.

clue.text: First mate cruelly imprisoned by senior officer in film style

indicators.note: imprisoned by means these pieces are locked inside the officer

parts.note: C-in-C, commander-in-chief, is a senior officer

indicators.note: cruelly suggests the letters of the word mate are treated roughly and rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, the first

explanation.surface: A first mate is cruelly locked up by a senior officer, film-style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cruelly' turns MATE into EMAT; with I (one) it goes inside CINC, 'imprisoned by' the commander-in-chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in the manner of the movies has a quality typical of motion pictures.

clue.text: This man's soul: next one out's a magpie

definitions.text: This man's soul: next one out's a magpie

parts.words: This man's soul: next one out's a magpie
parts.note: the soul; on a rifle target the ring just outside this one is called the magpie

explanation.surface: Someone describes a person's soul as next door to a thieving bird.
explanation.walkthrough: A shooting target's rings run bull, then this ring, then the magpie, then the outer.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner man is a phrase for the soul, and on a target this ring lies just inside the magpie.

clue.text: See 21
I can't think for myself: I'm following the cattle doctor

indicators.note: I am following means the letter for I comes after the other pieces

parts.note: a zo (also dzo or zho) is a Himalayan yak-cattle hybrid
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
'I am following' places the letter I after the rest

explanation.surface: Someone admits they have no mind of their own and simply trail after the vet.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the answer: a zombi is a mindless being, so it 'can't think for itself'.
explanation.definitionFit: A zombi is a reanimated corpse with no will of its own, so it has no independent thought.

clue.text: Gold backing — something wrong here stake for poor old horse

indicators.note: backing means the word for gold is read from back to front

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a sin is a wrongdoing
an ante is a stake put up in poker

explanation.surface: A gambler bets on a poor old horse and admits it may be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns OR round to RO. Rosinante is Don Quixote's broken-down nag in Cervantes's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Quixote's horse in Cervantes is a famously skinny, decrepit nag, and the name is used for any worn-out steed.

clue.text: Estimate with foreign currency stops above the line

parts.note: a quotation is a builder's or trader's estimate of cost
marks were the currency of Germany

explanation.surface: A price estimate given in foreign money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stops' means punctuation marks, as in full stop; these ones sit above the line of writing rather than on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Punctuation is called stops, and inverted commas are written high, above the baseline of the text.

clue.text: See 11
Finish with tail in the air?

explanation.surface: A question about how things finish when someone's rear is raised.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish somewhere is to land there eventually; and something with its tail up has its back end pointing skyward.

clue.text: Chairman in previous generation used to write on baking sheets?

definitions.text: used to write on baking sheets?

indicators.note: in means the chairman piece goes inside the generation piece

parts.note: a parent belongs to the generation before

explanation.surface: A chairman of the older generation writes on sheets used for baking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts CHM inside PARENT. The definition has two senses: old writing material made from animal skin, and baking paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Treated animal skin was the old writing surface, and greaseproof paper for lining baking trays bears the same name.

clue.text: Man painting stream causes unpleasant sensation

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
painting is a form of art
burn is the Scottish word for a stream

explanation.surface: An artist painting a stream finds it gives him an unpleasant feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigestion gives a burning feeling behind the breastbone, an unpleasant sensation.

clue.text: Emperor making a law with hesitation

parts.note: lex is Latin for law
and means with, together with
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An emperor lays down a law, but hesitantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great built a vast empire from Greece to India.

clue.text: Effect of the sun was fatal to those with blue collars

indicators.note: effect of is taken as what results from working on the word sun, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: something fatal to people killed them

explanation.surface: Sunstroke proved fatal to manual workers in the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Effect of' turns SUN into UNS. Blue-collar workers are manual labourers, here those without trade qualifications.
explanation.definitionFit: Manual workers without training or trade qualifications are classed as unqualified labour.

clue.text: River crossing by unusually tidy barge

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of the words beside it are set in an unusual new order

explanation.surface: A barge kept surprisingly neat crosses the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay Bridge spans the Firth of Tay in Scotland; its first version collapsed in 1879.
explanation.definitionFit: This bridge carries the railway across the estuary of Scotland's longest river at Dundee.

clue.text: Our cat's cruel to African birds

indicators.note: cruel suggests the letters of the words are roughly treated and rearranged

explanation.surface: A pet cat is cruel to African birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'cat's' is part of the fodder; 'to' is a link. Turacos are colourful fruit-eating birds of Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: These are brightly coloured fruit-eating birds of sub-Saharan forests, related to cuckoos.

clue.text: Effect of expensive suits on fellow goodies?

parts.note: co- means fellow, joint, as in co-worker
STS is short for saints, the goodies

explanation.surface: Smart tailoring has an effect on a colleague who likes to look good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suits' are lawsuits, not clothing: an expensive legal case leaves the loser paying the other side's bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing a lawsuit can leave a party ordered to pay the legal expenses, a heavy financial burden.

clue.text: South-East Brazilian city given to the Uncle Sam? You cannot be !

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian city
Uncle Sam personifies the US

explanation.surface: A Brazilian city handed over to America provokes disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a fill-in-the-blank: 'You cannot be serious!' is John McEnroe's famous protest to a tennis umpire.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase completes the tennis player's outburst of disbelief at an umpire's call, meaning 'surely you are joking'.

clue.text: American writer evoking the shallower name-drop

indicators.note: evoking is taken to mean calling up a new form, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer is mocked as one who drops names in a shallow way.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses all seventeen letters of SHALLOWER NAME-DROP; 'the' is a link. Emerson was the 19th-century American essayist and Transcendentalist.
explanation.definitionFit: This nineteenth-century New England essayist and poet led the Transcendentalist movement in the United States.

clue.text: Fast nothing! Just the opposite

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone protests that they are not fast at all, quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'Just the opposite' points back at 'Fast': the answer is the musical term for slow.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the tempo marking means slowly, the reverse of quick.

clue.text: Better off with salutation the FT changes round

parts.note: a newspaper speaks of itself as we, the editorial voice

indicators.note: round means one piece goes around another, holding it inside

parts.note: with we as subject, changes becomes the verb alter
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: Readers are richer thanks to a greeting the Financial Times rewrites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts HI inside ALTER, giving ALTHIER. The FT is 'we' in its own editorials, so 'the FT changes' reads as WE ALTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Having more money than before means being richer, in a more comfortable financial position.

clue.text: Mounted tank to increase pressure

parts.note: describes a reservoir raised high on a structure so gravity gives the supply pressure

explanation.surface: A tank set up high to boost pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tank' suggests a military vehicle, but it is a reservoir set on high supports.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised reservoir lets gravity push the supply through the mains at useful pressure.

clue.text: See 23
Joined up, deceived about shocking practice

indicators.note: about means one piece is placed around another, enclosing it

parts.note: to con is to deceive
ECT, electroconvulsive therapy, treats patients with electric shocks

explanation.surface: Someone tricked into signing up is caught out by a scandalous practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ECT inside CONNED. 'Shocking' means using electric shocks, not scandalous.
explanation.definitionFit: Things linked together or attached to one another are coupled, fastened together.

clue.text: See 21
Duck eats duck — this will get one moving

indicators.note: eats means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a scoter is a sea duck
a duck is a score of nothing, the letter O

explanation.surface: One duck swallows another, which gets something moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eats' puts O, a nil score in cricket, inside SCOTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A kick-scooter or motor scooter is a small vehicle for getting around.

clue.text: At the back of the fire you get very hot and awfully sore outside

definitions.text: At the back of the fire

indicators.note: outside means one piece is placed around another piece
awfully suggests the letters of the word sore are mangled into a new order

parts.note: something red-hot glows red

explanation.surface: Standing at the back of a fire leaves one very hot and sore all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' turns SORE into REOS, which goes 'outside' RED. A reredos is an altar screen, and also a fireback, the wall behind a hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is also the old name for a fireback, the iron or brick wall behind a hearth.
